name: Aloo Paratha
cuisine: North Indian (Punjabi), now an all-India home and dhaba staple, sold across Mumbai by tiffin services, Punjabi eateries and paratha specialists

ingredients.name: Whole wheat flour (atta), for dusting
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 heaped tbsp in a small plate

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.householdMeasure: 3½ tbsp (add a little at a time)

ingredients.name: Sunflower oil (or any neutral cooking oil), for the dough
Red chilli powder (lal mirch), Kashmiri or regular

equipment: Pressure cooker (2–3 litre) to boil the potato
Mixing bowl (parat or any wide bowl) for the dough
Flat spatula (turner) for flipping and pressing
Small spoon or silicone brush for spreading ghee
Damp cloth or plate to cover the resting dough
Measuring cup and spoons (a regular tea cup and teaspoons work as a stand-in)

steps.title: Wash the potato
steps.text: Rinse 160 g potato (1 large) under running water and rub off any soil.
steps.visualCue: Clean skin, no mud in the eyes
steps.cameraCheck: The washed potato in your hand
steps.videoShot: The potato under the running tap.

steps.title: Pressure-cook the potato
steps.text: Put the whole potato (halved if very large) in the cooker with 1 cup water. Close and cook on medium heat for 3 whistles, then switch off.
steps.tip: Do not over-boil. A watery, soggy potato makes a wet filling, which tears the paratha.
steps.visualCue: 3 whistles
steps.cameraCheck: The closed cooker on the flame
steps.videoShot: The cooker whistling.

steps.title: Measure the flour
steps.text: While the potato cooks, put 80 g (⅔ cup) whole wheat flour into the mixing bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small mound of flour
steps.cameraCheck: ⅔ cup atta in the bowl
steps.videoShot: Flour falling from the cup into the bowl.

steps.title: Add salt and oil to the flour
steps.text: Add a small pinch of salt and ½ tsp oil. Rub them in with your fingertips.
steps.visualCue: The flour looks very slightly crumbly where the oil went in.
steps.cameraCheck: The flour with oil rubbed in
steps.videoShot: Fingers rubbing the oil into the flour.

steps.title: Add the first part of the water
steps.text: Pour in about 35 ml (2½ tbsp) water and mix with your fingers.
steps.visualCue: Shaggy lumps form, with some dry flour left in the bowl.
steps.videoShot: Water pouring in, fingers mixing.

steps.title: Add the rest of the water slowly
steps.text: Add the remaining water 1 tsp at a time, only until all the flour comes together.
steps.tip: You may not need all 50 ml. Flours absorb water differently.
steps.visualCue: One rough ball, no dry flour left
steps.videoShot: A teaspoon of water going in, then the dough gathering.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Push the dough away with the heel of your palm, fold it back, turn it a quarter and repeat.
steps.visualCue: Smooth, soft and slightly springy. A finger pressed in leaves a dent that slowly fills back. It should be softer than roti dough but not sticky.
steps.videoShot: Hands kneading with a push-fold-turn rhythm.

steps.title: Rest the dough
steps.text: Cover the bowl with a damp cloth or a plate.
steps.visualCue: After resting, the dough feels softer and more relaxed.
steps.videoShot: The cloth being laid over the bowl.

steps.title: Release the pressure
steps.text: Let the cooker cool until the pressure drops by itself, then open it.
steps.visualCue: No hiss when you lift the weight
steps.cameraCheck: The open cooker with the potato
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting and steam rising.

steps.title: Check the potato
steps.text: Poke the potato with a knife.
steps.visualCue: The knife slides through easily with no hard centre.
steps.videoShot: The knife sliding in.

steps.title: Cool and peel the potato
steps.text: Move it to a plate. When cool enough to hold, peel off the skin.
steps.tip: Spread it out to cool faster. Warm filling releases steam and tears the dough.
steps.visualCue: Peeled potato, dry on the surface, only slightly warm
steps.cameraCheck: The peeled potato on the plate
steps.videoShot: The skin pulling away.

steps.title: Chop the green chilli
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small green chilli (5 g).
steps.visualCue: Tiny pieces, no long strips
steps.cameraCheck: The chopped chilli on the board
steps.videoShot: The knife chopping the chilli.

steps.title: Grate the ginger
steps.text: Peel and grate a ½ inch piece of ginger (3 g).
steps.visualCue: About 1 tsp of fine, juicy ginger paste
steps.videoShot: Ginger on the grater.

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Finely chop 5 g (1 tbsp) coriander leaves and pat them dry with a paper towel.
steps.visualCue: Fine, dry green flecks
steps.videoShot: The knife rocking through the leaves.

steps.title: Grate or mash the potato
steps.text: Grate the potato into the second bowl, or mash it with a masher until there are no lumps.
steps.tip: Lumps poke through the dough when you roll. Take the extra minute here.
steps.visualCue: Fine and smooth, no pieces bigger than a pea
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed potato in the bowl
steps.videoShot: The potato going through the grater.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp ajwain (crush it between your palms first), ½ tsp roasted cumin powder, ¼ tsp red chilli powder, ¼ tsp garam masala, ½ tsp amchur and ¼ tsp salt.
steps.visualCue: Little piles of coloured spice on the white potato
steps.cameraCheck: The spices on top of the potato
steps.videoShot: Each spice going in.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Add the chilli, ginger and coriander. Mix well with your fingers and taste.
steps.tip: It should taste a little saltier and tangier than you'd like, because the dough is bland.
steps.visualCue: Evenly speckled filling that holds together when squeezed but does not feel wet
steps.videoShot: Fingers mixing, then one squeeze.

steps.title: Divide the filling
steps.text: Shape the filling into 2 equal balls (about 80 g each).
steps.visualCue: 2 balls, each about the size of a lime, slightly bigger than the dough balls will be
steps.videoShot: Hands rolling the filling balls.

steps.title: Divide the dough
steps.text: Knead the rested dough for 10 seconds and split it into 2 equal parts. Roll each into a smooth ball.
steps.visualCue: 2 smooth balls with no cracks, each about the size of a small lime
steps.cameraCheck: 2 dough balls next to 2 filling balls
steps.videoShot: Dough being pinched in half and rolled.

steps.title: Heat the tawa
steps.text: Put the tawa on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sprinkled on it sizzle and vanish in 2–3 seconds.
steps.videoShot: Water drops sizzling on the tawa.

steps.title: Roll the first dough ball into a small disc
steps.text: Dust one dough ball with flour and roll it into a disc about 10 cm (4 inch) across, thicker in the centre than at the edges.
steps.visualCue: An even small circle
steps.videoShot: The rolling pin pressing out the disc.

steps.title: Stuff the disc
steps.text: Place one filling ball in the centre. Gently pleat the edges up and around the filling, like a pouch.
steps.visualCue: The filling is fully covered, with pleats meeting at the top.
steps.videoShot: Fingers pulling the pleats up.

steps.title: Seal the pouch
steps.text: Pinch the pleats together and twist off any extra dough at the top. Press the pouch flat with your palm, sealed side down.
steps.tip: If you see a crack, pinch a scrap of dough over it before rolling.
steps.visualCue: A flat, round patty with no filling showing
steps.videoShot: The palm pressing the patty flat.

steps.title: Roll the paratha
steps.text: Dust both sides with flour. Roll gently from the centre outwards, turning the paratha a quarter turn often, to about 18 cm (7 inch) across.
steps.tip: Light pressure only. If filling peeks out, dust that spot with flour and keep going, or stop at a slightly smaller size.
steps.visualCue: An even round about 3–4 mm thick, with the filling faintly visible but not breaking through
steps.cameraCheck: The rolled paratha next to a ruler or a 7 inch plate
steps.videoShot: The pin rolling outwards in short strokes, the paratha turning.

steps.title: First side on the tawa
steps.text: Dust off extra flour and lay the paratha on the hot tawa.
steps.visualCue: Small bubbles appear on top and the underside has light brown spots.
steps.videoShot: The paratha being laid down and bubbles forming.

steps.title: Flip it
steps.text: Turn the paratha over with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: The first side shows pale brown spots; the second side starts to dry.
steps.videoShot: The flip.

steps.title: Ghee the top
steps.text: Spread ½ tsp ghee over the top side.
steps.visualCue: A thin shine across the whole surface
steps.videoShot: The spoon spreading ghee in circles.

steps.title: Flip and press
steps.text: Flip again and press the edges and puffed areas gently with the spatula.
steps.visualCue: Sizzling, the paratha puffs in places and turns golden-brown with crisp spots.
steps.videoShot: The spatula pressing as the paratha puffs.

steps.title: Ghee the second side
steps.text: Spread the remaining ½ tsp ghee on top, flip once more and press until both sides are evenly golden.
steps.tip: If it browns before it cooks through, turn the flame down a little. A smoking-hot tawa burns the outside and leaves raw dough inside.
steps.visualCue: Both sides golden-brown with darker crisp spots, no raw white patches, edges cooked through
steps.cameraCheck: Both sides of the finished paratha
steps.videoShot: The final flip, showing an evenly golden paratha.

steps.title: Rest the first paratha
steps.text: Move it to a plate or a cloth-lined box.
steps.visualCue: Steam rises from the surface.
steps.videoShot: The paratha sliding onto the plate.

steps.title: Make the second paratha
steps.text: Repeat steps 21–30 with the second dough and filling ball.
steps.visualCue: A second paratha matching the first
steps.videoShot: The two parathas side by side.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut each paratha in half or quarters and plate with curd and pickle (and butter on top, if you like).
steps.visualCue: Golden wedges showing the yellow-speckled potato layer inside
steps.videoShot: A paratha being torn open to show the filling.

reasons: the home version uses whole wheat (about 13 g fibre per serving) and only 2 tsp ghee for 2 parathas, with no deep frying and no sugar. But it is mostly starch (about 94 g carbs from wheat plus potato), protein is modest (about 15 g), and there are almost no vegetables beyond the potato. Restaurant and dhaba parathas are often cooked with 1–2 tbsp ghee, oil or butter each, topped with a block of butter, made partly with maida, and served with salty pickle, so fat and sodium can double.

researchRating.basis: aloo paratha is one of the most-loved Indian breakfasts. It is widely described as Punjab's favourite breakfast and a comfort food, and recipe pages score very highly (4.97 from 86 votes on Hebbar's Kitchen, 4.94 from 16 on Cook with Manali, 4.89 from 42 on RecipeTin Eats, 4.75 on Manjula's Kitchen, 4.56 from 18 on Cook Click n Devour). Mumbai food guides (Homegrown, Curly Tales) list dedicated paratha spots across the city. Small deductions because it is heavy and greasy when made restaurant-style, and many home cooks report tearing and leaking filling.

storage: Cooked parathas keep in the fridge for up to 2 days, wrapped in foil or in an airtight box. To freeze, half-cook them (light spots on both sides, no ghee), cool, stack with butter paper between them and freeze for up to 1 month. Cook from frozen on a medium tawa with ghee, about 2 min per side. To reheat a fridge paratha, warm it on a hot tawa for 30–45 sec per side (crispier than the microwave). The raw potato filling keeps in the fridge for 1 day; the raw dough keeps for 1 day but darkens slightly.
leftoverRemix: Aloo paratha "chaat" wraps. Warm a leftover paratha on the tawa until crisp, spread 1 tbsp green chutney and 1 tbsp beaten curd, top with chopped onion, tomato, a pinch of chaat masala and a handful of sev, then roll it up tightly like a frankie. It makes a quick tiffin lunch.
burnOff: about 7.8 km of running (545 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 10.9 km of brisk walking (about 2 hr 10 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With butter, curd and pickle (about 690 kcal), about 9.9 km of running (est.).
